title: Q1. Left Rotate an Array by One Position
statement: Given an array of n integers, move the first element to the end and shift every other element one position to the left. Print the resulting array.

title: Q2. Common Elements of Two Arrays (No Duplicates)
statement: Given two arrays, print the distinct elements that occur in both arrays. Each common value must be printed only once, in the order in which it first appears in the first array. Print -1 if there are no common elements.

title: Q3. Find the Leaders in an Array
statement: An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The last element is always a leader. Given an array, print all leaders from left to right.

title: Q4. Difference Between the Second Maximum and Second Minimum
statement: Given an array containing at least two distinct values, find the second smallest distinct element and the second largest distinct element. Print second largest - second smallest. Duplicates do not create new ranks.

title: Q5. Left Rotate an Array by K Positions
statement: Given an array of n integers and an integer k, rotate the array to the left by k positions. Rotations wrap around, and k may be greater than n.

title: Q6. Maximum Sum Mountain Subarray
statement: A mountain subarray is a contiguous subarray with a strictly increasing part followed immediately by a strictly decreasing part. It must contain at least three elements and have a peak. Equal adjacent values break a mountain. Find the maximum sum, or print 0 if no mountain exists.

title: Q7. Maximum Length of a Mountain
statement: A mountain is a contiguous sequence that strictly increases for one or more steps, then strictly decreases for one or more steps. A peak is required. Equal adjacent values break a mountain. Find the longest mountain length, or print 0 if no mountain exists.

title: Q8. Gas Station Circuit
statement: There are n gas stations on a circular route. gas[i] is available at station i, and cost[i] is needed to travel to the next station. Find the starting station index for one complete trip, or print -1. Indices are zero-based.
